A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HandOS. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary material are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original HandOS evaluations on FreiHand, HO3Dv3, DexYCB, and HInt, alongside ablations and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original evaluations and adds loss ablations, detector substitution, ground-truth-box evaluation, and inference-efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: The frozen detector, side tuning, query expansion and lifting, hierarchical attention, and reconstruction losses remain unchanged. Calling the lifting matrix learnable clarifies the existing design; the DINO-X experiment tests another detector configuration without introducing a new reconstruction procedure.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation retain the same datasets and task coverage. CompHand and H2O3D extra-training data already appeared in v1's supplement. The added experiments test configurations and controls within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Comparison coverage is substantially reduced across three main benchmarks: Table 1 removes FastMETRO, FastViT, DeFormer, and AMVUR; Table 3 removes S2HAND, KeypointTransformer, and ArtiBoost; Table 4 removes A2J and METRO. v2 also adds an explicit efficiency comparison against ViTPose+HaMeR. The Hamba extra-data comparison now displayed in main Table 3 already existed in v1's appendix.

E3.justification: Existing training settings and benchmark metrics remain unchanged. New experiments introduce loss-removal controls, DINO-X substitution, HO3Dv3 inference using ground-truth boxes, and efficiency evaluation across person and hand counts; these are additional protocols rather than revisions to the original benchmark settings.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: Table VIII tests loss contributions, Table IX tests detector portability, and Table X adds a ground-truth-box robustness control. Sections XI–XII add qualitative comparisons with HaMeR and computational-efficiency analysis. The original attention, feature-selection, and failure analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experimental results.

E6.justification: Substantial new diagnostic and efficiency results are reported. Table VIII gives FreiHand PA-MPVPE of 5.6 mm with all losses versus 13.2 mm with the three tested loss groups omitted. Table IX adds DINO-X results; Table X adds ground-truth-box results of 8.4/8.5 mm PA-MPJPE/PA-MPVPE. Section XII reports FLOPs, memory, and latency. Removed baselines also remove result entries. Retained headline scores and the extra-training HO3Dv3 scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: No substantive definitions, derivations, assumptions, or proofs are added or revised. Equation 8 replaces inconsistent B notation with R for reference boxes, preserving the same operations; other mathematical changes clarify notation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: one-stage reconstruction without prerequisite handedness classification, the interactive 2D–3D decoder, and strong benchmark performance. Additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of OKS, structural, and normal-consistency losses, and attributes ground-truth-box robustness to deformable attention's adaptive localization. Existing limitations concerning geometry priors, rotational pose recovery, and temporal coherence remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Section XII newly identifies RTX3090 and PyTorch for inference measurements and supplies computational, memory, and timing information. v2 explicitly describes the lifting matrix as learnable and directs readers to the homepage for video results. Existing training recipes, loss weights, and A100 training costs are retained.

R1.justification: v2 introduces DINO-X as another detector supporting the framework's positioning, but its citation appears as an unresolved question mark. The related-work discussion and the 81 bibliography entries otherwise retain the same works and substantive positioning.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. v2 adds a supplementary abstract and sections for detector adaptation, qualitative comparison, and efficiency, switches supplementary numbering to Roman numerals, clarifies method terminology, and edits acknowledgments.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is revised to make query lifting more explicit, and its caption clarifies omitted reference boxes. v2 adds two supplementary tables and Figure X, revises benchmark-table row structures, and relocates Tables 5–6. Existing failure and qualitative galleries are preserved under new numbering and placement.

improvement.justification: The added loss ablations, detector test, ground-truth-box control, and efficiency measurements make the existing design and practical claims better supported and easier to assess. These gains outweigh the narrowed baseline tables and unresolved DINO-X citation. The core method, headline results, and stated limitations remain stable, so the overall improvement is limited.
